- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.15) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently underreacts to sharp sentiment reversals; if sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 3–8%.
- Overshoots after price spikes (especially >70) are common; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment > 0.2 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% per day.
- Mean reversion bias is evident in 30-day forecasts: if 10+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–4% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (±0.25 or more), reduce forecast confidence and apply ±2% buffer to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
